records.selection_criteria: Exploratory search for product safety recalls, certification enforcement and announced compliance operations during the study period in study countries, prioritizing products and components comparable to the supplied case-study descriptions. Include other brands as context without assuming a case-study supplier, product or shipment match.

sources_searched.outcome: Included a US recall for multi-styler hair dryers lacking immersion protection.
Included a robotic pool vacuum recall involving overheating adapters, as contextual rather than floor-vacuum evidence.
Included the reported Philippine confiscation of uncertified appliances, including fans; the release and webpage display different dates.
Included a model- and serial-specific US air-purifier recall.
Included a US bladeless heating and cooling fan recall.
Included a US recall involving specified cordless vacuum batteries, manufactured in China according to the notice.
Included reporting of a planned Malaysian electrical product compliance operation; no actual seizure or case-study impact inferred.
Reviewed an additional 2025 US hair dryer recall; not included in this initial selection.
Reviewed the ASEAN product-alert portal; the accessible rendered page did not expose a populated recall listing.
The accessible rendered Singapore recall page did not expose its full listing; no specific notice was verified.
The accessible rendered Taiwan recall page did not expose a usable listing; no specific notice was verified.

known_coverage_gaps: Searches are exploratory and not exhaustive across product types, recalls, suppliers, markets, languages or jurisdictions. No Singapore, Taiwan or Chinese domestic recall was verified in this pass.
The US notices describe US recalls even where products or batteries were manufactured in China; they do not prove recalls or sales in other countries.
A model number is not an HS code or verified graph product identifier. Named importers, distributors and manufacturers are source roles, not verified Dyson suppliers.
The Philippine report's stated release date and webpage date differ; the operation date, fan-only quantity and final legal outcome are unknown.
Malaysia's operation was planned when reported, not a verified seizure or recall. A lack of certification markings does not alone establish a failed safety test.

Recall announcement dates, defect onset, individual incidents, remedy completion, supplier production and shipment delays are distinct; retrieval windows do not establish a continuous disruption or recovery duration.
No record verifies an affected case-study shipment, product, supplier or calibrated disruption probability.

records.selection_criteria: Exploratory search for route chokepoint impacts, security warnings and planned constraints during the study period, prioritizing routes potentially relevant to the six study countries. Include clearly labelled external corridor context without asserting that any case-study shipment used it.

sources_searched.outcome: Included UNCTAD's early-May Suez transit-tonnage comparison against the 2023 average and reported Cape routing.
Reviewed UNCTAD's summary of its 2025 maritime transport report and route diversion.
Included a reviewed security alert on three reported sea robberies in Singapore Strait; no channel closure or route-wide delay inferred.
Included Taiwan's navigation warnings and assessment of commercial port movements during military exercises.
Reviewed additional reporting on designated live-fire exercise areas and Taiwan's maritime warning.
Included UNCTAD's early-March comparison of Hormuz vessel transits as reported by UN News; formal closure was not reported.
Reviewed UNCTAD's 10 March rapid assessment for disruption context.
Reviewed IEA reporting of near-halted tanker movement, also referenced by related geopolitical evidence.
Included the canal authority's planned Gatun east-lane maintenance and Panamax booking limits; implementation not independently confirmed.
Additional canal notice returned HTTP 403 and was not reviewed.
Carrier Red Sea update timed out and was not independently reviewed.
Carrier later update timed out and was not independently reviewed.
Reviewed an unrelated Singapore Strait boarding notice, which expressly says navigation was not affected; no separate closure record added.

known_coverage_gaps: Searches are exploratory and not exhaustive across routes, countries, event types, vessel classes, dates or sources. A missing record is not proof of an unaffected route.
Suez, Hormuz and Panama are outside the six study countries and are included as unverified route context. Empty incident country arrays do not establish an absence of geography or a case-study match.

The Singapore Strait label identifies a corridor rather than the jurisdiction of each reported robbery. Neither the robberies nor Taiwan navigation warnings establish route-wide closures or shipment delays.
The Suez statistic concerns tonnage relative to the 2023 average, not vessel count; the Hormuz statistic concerns ship transits and does not establish a formal closure.

Gatun maintenance, slot limits and subsequent reinstatement were scheduled, not independently verified as completed. Conditions, recovery dates and impact outside documented observations remain unknown.
No record verifies an affected case-study vessel, product, shipment or route. Linked geopolitical evidence can describe the same event; avoid double counting.
Search windows are candidate retrieval aids, not continuous disruption intervals, shipment delays or calibrated recovery estimates.

Approximated values are listed in each record's `approximations` field and are unreviewed analyst approximations, not source facts. Suez and Panama trade lanes (Asian study countries to US East and Gulf coast ports) and the Hormuz Singapore country link do not establish that any case-study shipment used or was affected by the corridor.

known_coverage_gaps: Searches are exploratory and not exhaustive across suppliers, entities, countries, registries, languages or dates; no conclusion of financial health follows from an absent record.
The V.S. Industry group loss is a financial-pressure indicator, not evidence of insolvency, default or an inability to meet obligations. Its underlying exchange filing was not independently reviewed.

The initial Chapter 11 plans and claims about business continuity are company statements, and selected legal emergence announcements do not establish uninterrupted supply or complete stakeholder recovery.
No record verifies an affected case-study shipment, customer order, production outage or calibrated insolvency probability. Search buffers are not disruption durations.

No record establishes an incident, its probability, continuous exposure, a graph match, a current supplier relationship, or an affected Dyson shipment. Source estimates and calculation methods are not interchangeable.

records.selection_criteria: Exploratory manual collection of selected US import tariff measures affecting study-country origins, prioritizing changing 2025–2026 country rates and a product-specific lithium-ion battery measure. Record separate legal layers, date windows, exact scope and exclusions; do not infer actual origin, classification, duties paid or case-study shipment exposure.

sources_searched.outcome: Reviewed the original China IEEPA 10% duty and start and in-transit conditions.
Reviewed the increase of the China synthetic-opioid duty from 10% to 20%.
Reviewed CBP guidance confirming the China duty's 4 March 2025 increase, exceptions and special in-transit cutoff.
Reviewed the change of that separate China duty from 20% to 10% for covered entries from 10 November 2025.
Reviewed EO 14326 country annex and the default 10% baseline for countries not listed.
Reviewed Annex II's Malaysia, Philippines and Taiwan reciprocal duty provisions and in-transit exception.
Reviewed CBP guidance for 7 August 2025 rates, exceptions and separate China treatment.
Reviewed EO 14389 termination of specified IEEPA duties, which did not terminate Section 301 or Section 232 duties.
Reviewed CBP's 24 February 2026 IEEPA collection cutoff; historical liability and refunds are not resolved.
Reviewed Section 122 10% surcharge, its effective and scheduled end times and exception categories.
Reviewed CBP Section 122 implementation and entry-specific exemptions.
Reviewed the USTR 2024 determination and scheduled 2026 25% China-origin lithium-ion battery tariff under 9903.91.06.
Reviewed Federal Register publication date and schedule of effective years for the 2024 USTR determination.
Reviewed the official account of the Supreme Court's IEEPA decision and the Taiwan agreement's implementation status as of May 2026.
Reviewed reporting that 10-digit battery reporting suffixes changed in 2026; avoid assuming the earlier suffix applies to all later entries.
Reviewed extension of 178 specific China Section 301 exclusions; no particular case-study item was matched.
Reviewed the USTR action on 60 economies and the distinction between flat and net-of-MFN rates.
Reviewed CBP implementation of the July 2026 Section 301 duties for all five non-US study origins, including Taiwan's conditional rate and exceptions.
Reviewed implementing Chapter 99 headings and exception lists for the July 2026 Section 301 action.
Reviewed secondary description of Section 122 expiry and transition to the distinct July 2026 Section 301 action.

known_coverage_gaps: This is not a comprehensive tariff schedule or legal-history review. April–July 2025 China escalation, earlier reciprocal transitions, foreign retaliatory duties, Section 232 and many commodity-specific rules are not comprehensively recorded.

No shipment, country of origin, entry time, complete HTSUS classification, exclusion, customs value or actual duty paid is verified. Null origin in the global Section 122 record indicates broad coverage, not that origin is irrelevant to all exclusions.

Rates are separate legal layers, not all-in rates. Stacking, exclusions and in-transit treatment must be determined for the precise entry; the Taiwan combined-rate target is not an additional flat 10% or an all-duties cap.

Country-rate dates mark nominal provisions and collection cutoffs, not a finding of legal validity: the Supreme Court held that IEEPA did not authorize the tariffs. Product-specific amendments, litigation and refunds require further review. A null effective end and a study-bounded search window do not prove continuous unchanged legal coverage.
The July 2026 Section 301 action concerns country-level investigated policies and does not establish forced labor at any named supplier or in any specific product.
US destination is studied here; trade between other countries, other tariff rates and actual origin determinations remain uncovered.
records.licence_notes: Store concise factual summaries and source links; verify source permissions before redistributing source documents.
records.review_method: Manually review official orders, annexes, USTR determinations and CBP entry guidance; separately identify legal measures, origin scope, commodity codes, rates, exclusions and date or time boundaries. Retain nulls and explicit limitations when applicability or expiry is unverified. Refresh the evidence-file hash after changes.
